hypothesis: Bright compact or elongated material and adjacent bright-to-dark interfaces
qualification: Broad material response, no specific anatomical label
observation: Bright elongated material and adjoining gray-to-dark boundaries recur in all four high-response patients, with weaker maps in lower ranks.

hypothesis: Localized texture responses among thin bright branching structures in dark regions
qualification: Peak can be in neighboring dark tissue; requires orthogonal inspection
observation: Localized responses recur among branching structures and surrounding dark texture. Orthogonal views show peaks in both gray structures and neighboring dark areas; a specific structure label is unresolved.

hypothesis: Gray or bright material on the dense side of a dense-to-dark interface
observation: The dense side of gray-to-dark boundaries responds in all four high-response patients. Boundary orientation affects response strength.

hypothesis: Broad dark textured regions, strongest near native axis-0 plane 2
qualification: Marked crop-position dependence; unsuitable for position-independent content labeling
observation: Dark regions respond broadly, but the four strongest confirmation peaks all occupy native axis-0 plane 2. Use as a position-conditioned control.

hypothesis: Localized internal dark-texture responses near thin bright structures
qualification: Full grid has strong boundary-band responses; interior-only description
observation: Interior peaks highlight local dark texture near brighter structures. Full-grid strongest responses occupy a fixed crop band, so whole-grid maxima cannot be interpreted with the interior description.

hypothesis: Very bright elongated material and strong dense-to-dark transitions
observation: Very bright compact or elongated structures recur in all four high-response patients. Discovery also contains a strong black-padding interface response.

hypothesis: Elongated bright material and adjacent gray-to-dark boundaries
observation: Elongated bright material and adjoining dense-to-dark boundaries recur in all four high-response patients.

hypothesis: Broad dark textured regions with reduced response in dense gray material
qualification: Spatial response has visible position dependence; broad low-density descriptor
observation: Broad dark textured regions respond in all four high-response patients; bright structures are relatively suppressed. Position modulation remains visible. The weakest confirmation response is above the weakest discovery responses.

qualification: Includes source-image support boundaries; discovery top patient has a black padding interface
observation: Bright-to-dark interfaces recur across four high-response patients. The discovery set also demonstrates sensitivity to black-padding interfaces.

hypothesis: Broad gray or bright material, with reduced activity in dark textured regions
observation: Broad gray material responds in all four high-response patients; the lowest-ranked dark-texture case has zero interior activity.

hypothesis: Gray material adjoining elongated bright structures and their dark interfaces
observation: Broad gray-to-dark interfaces recur, but elongated very bright structures do not consistently accompany the four strongest confirmation responses. The more specific discovery hypothesis is not confirmed.

hypothesis: Oriented elongated bright interfaces and strong material transitions
observation: Oriented elongated bright interfaces recur across the four high-response patients. The discovery set also demonstrates padding-interface sensitivity.

hypothesis: Dark-side band next to a bright curved interface
observation: The dark-side band next to a curved bright interface recurs across all four high-response patients. Lower-response images have weaker or discontinuous maps.
